There is a small ambiguity in the notation “variation.” I will first interpret \(Var[X]_t\) as the **pathwise total variation** of \(X\) on \([0,t]\), since no word “quadratic” is used. I will then note the quadratic-variation and variance interpretations.

### Total variation interpretation

A standard Brownian motion has continuous sample paths almost surely. Fix \(t\ge 0\) and restrict to the event where \(W\) is continuous on \([0,t]\). Then the map

\[
s\mapsto X_s=\int_0^s W_u\,du
\]

is continuously differentiable on \([0,t]\), with derivative

\[
X'_s = W_s.
\]

For a \(C^1\) function \(F\) on \([0,t]\), its total variation is

\[
\int_0^t |F'(s)|\,ds.
\]

Therefore,

\[
Var[X]_t
=
\sup_{0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=t}
\sum_{i=1}^n |X_{t_i}-X_{t_{i-1}}|
=
\int_0^t |W_s|\,ds
\qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

To see why this is finite: because \(W\) is continuous on the compact interval \([0,t]\),

\[
M_t:=\sup_{0\le s\le t}|W_s|<\infty
\qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

Hence

\[
Var[X]_t
=
\int_0^t |W_s|\,ds
\le t\,M_t
<\infty
\qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

In fact, it is even finite in mean:

\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^t |W_s|\,ds\right]
=
\int_0^t \mathbb{E}|W_s|\,ds
=
\int_0^t \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\pi}}\,ds
=
\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,t^{3/2}
<\infty.
\]

---

If by \(Var[X]_t\) you meant the **quadratic variation** \([X]_t\), then because \(X\) is a finite-variation continuous process, its quadratic variation is zero:

\[
[X]_t = 0.
\]

Indeed, for any partition \(\Pi\) with mesh going to zero,

\[
\sum_{i} (X_{t_i}-X_{t_{i-1}})^2
\le
\left(\max_i |X_{t_i}-X_{t_{i-1}}|\right)
\sum_i |X_{t_i}-X_{t_{i-1}}|,
\]

and the first factor tends to \(0\) by uniform continuity of \(X\), while the second is bounded by the finite total variation.

If instead you meant the **variance** of the random variable \(X_t\), then since \(X_t\) is centered and

\[
\mathbb{E}[W_sW_u]=\min(s,u),
\]

we get

\[
\operatorname{Var}(X_t)
=
\int_0^t\int_0^t \min(s,u)\,ds\,du
=
\frac{t^3}{3}.
\]

Thus, under the total-variation interpretation,

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
\text{Total variation: }\operatorname{Var}[X]_t=\int_0^t |W_s|\,ds<\infty\ \text{a.s.}\\
\text{If quadratic variation was intended: }[X]_t=0.\\
\text{If variance of }X_t\text{ was intended: }\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=\dfrac{t^3}{3}.
\end{gathered}
}
\]
